**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred level) — no redline proposed.**

- **No restriction on IBM.** Targeted searches for competing-product covenants, exclusivity, sole-source/requirements purchasing, and field-of-use or territory limits returned nothing binding IBM.
- **§ 14.18 (Restrictions and Limitations)** runs the other way — it limits MSL's use of IBM property and protects IBM's customer delivery schedules. That benefits us, so it is not flagged.
- **§ 5.1(v)** (acquisition by a direct competitor) is a mutual change-of-control *termination trigger*, not a covenant on what businesses IBM may operate or what products it may buy or build; it is out of scope for NONCOMPETE.
- **CDA freedom-to-compete language (p1490–p1491)** affirmatively preserves the Recipient's right to provide competitive products/services and to serve the Discloser's competitors, confirming the preferred position on its face.

The single preferred element ("Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction") is mapped as already met against that verbatim CDA text.
